choices.text: Physical access control to the data center where the storage servers are located

choices.label: B
choices.text: Physical data disposal procedures for storage devices at the end of their lives

choices.label: C
choices.text: Security of the underlying software and hypervisor that run the S3 service

choices.label: D
choices.text: Policies that determine who can access buckets and objects, and public access settings

explanation: The correct answer is the access policies and public access settings of buckets and objects. Security in the cloud is the customer's responsibility, and the customer decides who is allowed to access data. Physical access control to data centers is security of the cloud itself and is AWS's responsibility. Disposal of storage devices at the end of their lives is also an infrastructure area that AWS handles. The security of the underlying software and the hypervisor that run S3 is likewise a software layer managed by AWS, so it is not an item the customer is responsible for. Looking at the added conditions in the question, access policies and public access settings are security in the cloud, so they are the customer's responsibility.

prompt: A video encoding batch job runs on Amazon EC2 for 6 hours every night. The job saves its progress periodically, so it can resume even if an instance is reclaimed in the middle of a run. The start time is flexible, and the instances are not needed after the job finishes. Which EC2 purchasing option is the MOST cost-effective?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use On-Demand Instances, turning them on only for the hours needed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use Spot Instances to take advantage of spare capacity at a low price.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Purchase a 3-year Compute Savings Plans commitment and apply it to total usage.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reserve a Dedicated Host and use the entire physical server exclusively.

explanation: Spot Instances is the correct answer. Spot Instances is an option that uses spare EC2 capacity at a price much lower than On-Demand, and it suits flexible, interruption-tolerant workloads such as batch jobs that can resume after an interruption. On-Demand is flexible but charged at the standard price, so it is not the cheapest. A 3-year Savings Plans commitment applies a long-term commitment to a job that runs only 6 hours a day and does not take advantage of the interruption-tolerant condition. A Dedicated Host is an option needed for licensing or regulatory reasons and has the highest cost. Looking at the added conditions in the question, the job is flexible and interruption-tolerant, so Spot is the cheapest.

prompt: A mobile game sees traffic grow sharply and then fall with each event. It must read and write player session information quickly by key, and it does not want to plan capacity in advance or manage servers. The marketing team changes the event schedule often and does not announce it in advance. Which database is the MOST suitable?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Reserve a large Amazon RDS instance in advance to match peak event traffic.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Store the session information in an Amazon Redshift cluster and query it when needed.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Install a self-managed database on Amazon EC2 and add nodes manually.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use Amazon DynamoDB in on-demand capacity mode.

explanation: DynamoDB on-demand mode is the correct answer. It is a serverless NoSQL database that delivers single-digit millisecond performance, and on-demand mode automatically adjusts throughput to the request volume, so no capacity planning or server management is needed and you are billed for the requests you make. If you size RDS in advance for peak event traffic, money is wasted during normal times and you still have to manage the instance yourself. Redshift is an analytics warehouse and does not suit low-latency session lookups. A self-managed database on EC2 requires you to scale and operate nodes yourself, so it has the greatest operational burden. Looking at the added conditions in the question, unpredictable traffic and key-based access fit DynamoDB on-demand.

prompt: A compliance officer is building a control responsibility table for the AWS shared responsibility model. The officer wants to choose two examples of shared controls, in which both AWS and the customer are responsible in their own areas. Items that are solely AWS's responsibility or solely the customer's responsibility will be listed separately in other columns of the table. (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Patch management, in which AWS is responsible for the infrastructure and the customer is responsible for the guest operating system and applications

choices.label: B
choices.text: Configuration management, in which AWS is responsible for infrastructure devices and the customer is responsible for its own operating system and database settings

choices.label: C
choices.text: Security configuration of the AWS hypervisor and hardware firmware

choices.label: D
choices.text: Physical and environmental controls of the data center facilities

choices.label: E
choices.text: Classification of customer data and design of service access permissions

explanation: The correct answers are patch management and configuration management. Both are shared controls in which AWS is responsible for the infrastructure side and the customer is responsible for its own guest operating system, applications, and settings. Physical controls of data center facilities are inherited controls, in which the customer inherits AWS's controls as they are, so they are not shared. Data classification and access permission design are customer specific controls for which the customer alone is responsible. The configuration of the hypervisor and hardware firmware is an area for which AWS alone is responsible, so it is not a shared item. Looking at the added conditions in the question, the shared controls in which both sides are responsible for their own areas are patch management and configuration management.

prompt: Some applications at a financial company cannot move customer data out of the company's own data center because of regulations. In the migration plan, the company decided to exclude these applications from the scope of this migration and to review them again later. The services continue to operate, and there is no plan to decommission them. Which strategy does this correspond to?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Relocate, which moves to a different account or Region

choices.label: B
choices.text: Repurchase, which replaces the application with a cloud product

choices.label: C
choices.text: Retain, which leaves the application in its original environment as it is

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rehost, which moves servers without changes

explanation: The correct answer is retain, which leaves the application in its original environment as it is. A situation in which regulations prevent data from being moved out and the application will be reviewed again later is a typical retain case caused by data residency requirements. Relocate moves workloads between VPCs, Regions, or accounts, or to a cloud version of a platform, so the data would leave the environment and violate the regulation. Repurchase is a strategy that replaces a product and does not resolve the restriction on moving data. Rehost moves servers to AWS as they are, so the data would also leave the company's premises. Looking at the added conditions in the question, the applications are left as they are rather than moved and are not decommissioned, so this is retain.

prompt: A team uploads container images to Amazon ECR and runs its service on Amazon EC2 instances. The team wants to continuously and automatically check whether newly published CVEs affect its images and instances, without creating a manual scan schedule. Several dozen instances are already in operation, so the team cannot check them one by one. Which service is the MOST suitable?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amazon GuardDuty

choices.label: B
choices.text: Amazon Inspector

choices.label: C
choices.text: Amazon Macie

choices.label: D
choices.text: AWS Shield

explanation: The correct answer is Amazon Inspector. Inspector automatically discovers EC2 instances, ECR container images, and Lambda functions, continuously scans them for software vulnerabilities, and reassesses them when a new CVE is published. GuardDuty is a service that analyzes logs to detect threat activity, which is different from software vulnerability scanning. Macie is a service that finds sensitive information in S3 data. Shield is a service that protects against DDoS attacks and has nothing to do with checking CVEs. Looking at the added conditions in the question, the service that automatically and continuously scans for software vulnerabilities is Inspector.

prompt: A small development team wants AWS to handle EC2 provisioning, load balancing, automatic scaling, and health monitoring just by uploading its Java web application code. All team members have little infrastructure design experience, and this application behaves dynamically. Which service has the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: AWS Elastic Beanstalk, a service that automatically configures the environment when you upload code

choices.label: B
choices.text: AWS CloudFormation, a service that creates resources according to templates that you write yourself

choices.label: C
choices.text: Amazon EC2 and Auto Scaling, in which you design and configure the load balancer yourself

choices.label: D
choices.text: Amazon S3 static website hosting, which serves only static files

explanation: Elastic Beanstalk is the correct answer. When you upload the application source, it provisions EC2 instances and configures load balancing, health monitoring, and automatic scaling, and it supports several platforms including Java. There is no additional charge for the service itself, and you pay only for the underlying resources. CloudFormation requires you to design templates yourself, which is a heavy burden for a team with little experience. Configuring EC2 and Auto Scaling yourself leaves the entire design to the team. S3 static hosting cannot run server code, so it does not suit a Java web application. Looking at the added conditions in the question, the service that configures the environment from just a code upload is Elastic Beanstalk, and a dynamic application does not fit static hosting.

prompt: After a startup created its AWS account, the CEO signs in as the root user and deploys the service every day. The company has grown to five employees who need to share the deployments, and a recent external security review flagged this practice. Which action improves the security of the account the MOST?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Turn on MFA for the root user and lock it away, and perform day-to-day tasks as separate users that have only the required permissions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create access keys for the root user and store them in the deployment tool for automation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Share the root user password with the whole team but change it every month.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Copy the root user permissions to an administrators group and let all developers use it.

explanation: The correct answer is to turn on MFA for the root user and lock it away, and perform day-to-day tasks as separate users that have only the required permissions. The root user has full permissions for the whole account, so the best practice is to strengthen its protection and not use it for daily work. Creating root access keys and storing them in a tool puts the entire account at risk if they leak. If the team shares the password, you cannot trace who did what, and the risk of exposure increases. Copying root permissions to a group and giving them to everyone directly contradicts the principle of least privilege. Looking at the added conditions in the question, the best practice is to lock the root user with MFA and do daily work with least-privilege users.

prompt: A company that has created a new AWS environment wants to choose measures that conform to IAM best practices at a security review meeting. The application runs on Amazon EC2, and the team has 10 members. Someone suggested loosening security controls for the sake of development speed. Which TWO measures should be applied? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Grant the administrator policy to all developers and find problems afterward through the AWS CloudTrail records.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Require MFA for the root user and IAM users.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use temporary credentials from an IAM role, instead of long-term access keys, for applications that run on Amazon EC2.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Commit access keys to the source repository so that team members can easily pick them up and use them.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Have all team members share one IAM user's credentials for convenience.

explanation: The correct answers are using temporary credentials from an IAM role and requiring MFA. A role means that you do not need to distribute long-term keys, and MFA requires additional authentication even if a password leaks, which protects the root user and IAM users. Granting administrator permissions to everyone and finding problems afterward from records is not prevention and goes against the principle of least privilege. Committing access keys to a repository greatly increases the risk of leaks. Sharing one user makes it impossible to tell who performed an action and makes it hard to revoke individual permissions. Looking at the added conditions in the question, MFA and temporary credentials from roles are best practices, while sharing keys and excessive permissions are not.

prompt: A game company builds a new environment in the Japan Region to reduce latency for users in Japan, and the development team wants to bring up test environments in minutes instead of waiting for days. Which TWO cloud benefits correspond directly to these two actions, respectively? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deploying to multiple Regions around the world in minutes to serve users from places close to them

choices.label: B
choices.text: Scaling resources up and down to match demand without guessing the required capacity in advance

choices.label: C
choices.text: Trading fixed expense for variable expense by paying only for what you use without up-front investment

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gaining broader physical control over the data centers that you operate yourself

choices.label: E
choices.text: Agility, which provisions resources in minutes and reduces the time needed for experimentation and development

explanation: The correct answers are the benefit of deploying to multiple Regions in minutes and the agility of provisioning resources in minutes. Building a new environment in the Japan Region to reduce latency corresponds to the benefit of deploying quickly anywhere in the world, and bringing up test environments in minutes instead of days corresponds to agility. Trading fixed expense for variable expense is a real advantage, but it is not what the two actions address. Stopping guessing capacity is also a real benefit, but the two actions in the passage have nothing to do with scaling up and down to match demand. Broader physical control is not a benefit of the cloud and is the opposite of AWS operating the facilities. Looking at the added conditions in the question, adding a Region is global deployment, and creating environments in minutes is agility.

prompt: When an order is placed, the inventory service, the shipping service, and the notification service must all receive the same event. The publisher wants to send the message only once, and each service should process it independently. More subscribing services may be added in the future, and the company does not want to modify the publishing code each time. Which configuration has the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create one Amazon SQS queue and have the three services each pull messages from the same queue.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Write code so that the publishing service sends a request directly to the address of each of the three services.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Publish the message once to an Amazon SNS topic and connect each service as a subscriber.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Configure the three services to periodically read an Amazon S3 bucket to check for new objects.

explanation: Creating an SNS topic and subscribing each service to it is the correct answer. When the publisher sends to the topic once, SNS replicates and delivers the message to multiple subscribers such as SQS queues, Lambda functions, and HTTP endpoints in a fanout structure. If the services share the same SQS queue, each message is taken by only one consumer, which violates the condition that all three services receive the same event. If the publisher calls the services directly, the code must be changed every time a service is added. Polling S3 introduces delay and is inappropriate for delivering events. Looking at the added conditions in the question, fanout, in which a message is published once and delivered to multiple subscribers, is what an SNS topic provides.

prompt: A financial company's core system requires that, when a failure occurs, a designated technical account manager (TAM) is assigned to help the operations staff, and that urgent cases in which a business-critical system is down receive a response within 15 minutes. The budget is limited, so the company wants the lowest tier that satisfies these conditions. Which is the lowest-tier AWS Support plan that meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enterprise Support, which provides a designated TAM and a 15-minute response

choices.label: B
choices.text: Basic Support, which supports account and billing inquiries and service limit increases

choices.label: C
choices.text: Business Support+, which provides 24/7 access to AWS experts and targets a response within 30 minutes for business-critical cases

choices.label: D
choices.text: AWS Unified Operations, which provides a designated TAM and domain-specific engineers

explanation: Enterprise Support is the correct answer. It provides a designated TAM and a response within 15 minutes for business-critical system down cases, and it is the lowest-tier plan that meets the requirements. Basic Support supports only account and billing inquiries and service limit increases and has no technical support cases. Business Support+ provides 24/7 access to AWS experts, but its response target for business-critical cases is 30 minutes and it has no designated TAM, so it does not satisfy the 15-minute criterion or the TAM requirement. Unified Operations also provides a TAM but is a higher-tier plan, so it does not match the condition of the lowest tier. Looking at the added conditions in the question, the lowest tier that satisfies both a TAM and a 15-minute response is Enterprise Support.

prompt: A call center wants to convert thousands of call recording files per day into text for analysis. The team has no staff to train machine learning models itself, and the converted text will be used later for separate analysis. Which service is the MOST suitable for converting speech to text with an already trained managed AI service?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amazon Polly, a service that synthesizes text into human-sounding speech

choices.label: B
choices.text: Amazon Transcribe, a service that converts audio files to text

choices.label: C
choices.text: Amazon Rekognition, a service that analyzes objects and faces in images and videos

choices.label: D
choices.text: Amazon Comprehend, a service that extracts sentiment and key phrases from text

explanation: Amazon Transcribe is the correct answer. It is a managed service that converts speech to text, so you do not need to build machine learning models yourself. Polly does the opposite and turns text into speech. Rekognition is a service that analyzes images and videos, so it does not suit audio input. Comprehend analyzes data that is already text, so it cannot replace the first step of converting speech to text. Analyzing the converted text with Comprehend can be used as the next step. Looking at the added conditions in the question, the pretrained service that converts speech to text is Transcribe.

prompt: A startup has decided to move its on-premises servers to AWS. Because it has not yet created any AWS resources, it has no usage history, and it wants to estimate the monthly cost in advance for each Amazon EC2 and Amazon RDS configuration proposal and report it to executives. The report is due this week. Which tool is the MOST suitable to meet the requirement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use AWS Cost Explorer to view past usage costs and check future costs.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Set a budget in AWS Budgets and receive an alert when spending is exceeded.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enable the AWS Cost and Usage Report and review detailed billing information.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use AWS Pricing Calculator to enter the configuration for each service and calculate the estimated cost.

explanation: AWS Pricing Calculator is the correct answer. It is a tool for estimating cost by entering services and configurations before creating resources, so it suits a report made before the migration. Cost Explorer analyzes costs and usage that have already been incurred, so it has no underlying data when there are no resources yet. Budgets sends alerts when spending exceeds a threshold and does not estimate configuration proposals. The Cost and Usage Report is also detailed billing data that appears after actual use, so it cannot be used for advance estimates. Looking at the added conditions in the question, Pricing Calculator fits estimates before resource creation, and the others require existing usage history.

prompt: A product detail page repeats the same database query thousands of times per second, so the load on the database is high. The query results change only once every few minutes. The company wants to keep frequently read results in memory to speed up responses while leaving the existing database as it is and minimizing changes to the application structure. Which service is the MOST suitable to meet the requirement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Store frequently queried results in an in-memory cache by using Amazon ElastiCache.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add an Amazon Redshift cluster and configure it to process all query requests in a distributed manner.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Store the query results in Amazon S3 Glacier and restore them for every request.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Migrate the entire database to Amazon DynamoDB and redesign the table structure.

explanation: Amazon ElastiCache is the correct answer. It is a distributed in-memory cache service that stores frequently read results in memory to speed up responses and reduce the load on the source database, and the existing database can be left as it is. Redshift is an analytics warehouse and does not act as a cache for real-time lookups. Glacier is for long-term archiving, so restoring results for every request would make responses extremely slow. Migrating everything to DynamoDB violates the condition of keeping the database and also requires major application changes. Looking at the added conditions in the question, ElastiCache reduces database load for repeated queries whose results do not change often.
